name: Qatar

campaign_state.basis: Attacks on energy facilities in Qatar were reported in 2026. No end to the wider war is reported, so the classification is uncertain, and uncertain is treated as active.
campaign_state.limitation: One status search per system, in English, on the date checked. A search that returns no recent report does not show that none occurred. Iteration 20 added four conflict-level searches (the wider war, the Gulf states as a group, Iraq). None reported an end of the war, and renewed hostilities were reported in the autumn of 2026. No facility was looked up.

no_index_reason: Only the Russia-theatre system has a disruption index. Its weights and recovery assumptions were designed for that theatre and are not transferred to other countries, so this page shows reported disruptions and national energy context instead. No index is not a zero.

sectors.reason: A national capacity total and annual throughput are published, but the country has two refineries, so a share of capacity affected would be the status of a named plant. Shown as national context only.
sectors.label: Refining

sectors.reason: Denominator ready: the utility publishes contracted generating capacity annually on one basis under an open licence. Not scored: no outage reporting exists, the list of plants is short, and events resolve to country level. No model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).
sectors.label: Electric generation

sectors.reason: National aggregates only; the event-burden measure does not fit, and no grid detail is collected.
sectors.label: Transmission burden

sectors.reason: No inventory is built: it would centre on export routing, which is out of scope. National crude export volume is shown as context.
sectors.label: Oil logistics & export

sectors.reason: National LNG capacity and annual LNG exports are published and shown as context. Liquefaction is concentrated in very few places, so a share of capacity affected would be the status of particular facilities. Train-level capacity is never recorded.
sectors.label: Gas

sectors.reason: Not applicable: EIA marks coal production and consumption for Qatar as not applicable and shows no coal in power generation. The sector does not exist here, which is different from unknown.
sectors.label: Coal

reporting_environment_text: Disruption is disclosed mainly through company and ministry statements, usually only when material to investors or the state.
reporting_note: The state energy company, the state electricity and water utility and the ministry disclose disruption through statements, mostly carried by the state news agency. No body publishes an outage register or reliability statistics, so the coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: Qatar has 8 municipalities today; Natural Earth draws 7, on the arrangement before Al-Shahaniya was separated from Al Rayyan in 2014. Qatar is small and several municipalities hold a single large energy complex, so kinetic or security events default to COUNTRY level. A non-conflict event uses a municipality only where a safety reviewer finds it non-identifying. Offshore events are country level.

rulings.note: Doha. The name in the map file is Natural Earth's, which calls it Ad Dawhah.
Natural Earth names it Al Khawr; the official name is Al Khor and Al Thakhira.
Natural Earth names it Madinat ach Shamal; the official name is Al Shamal.

Drawn on its pre-2014 extent, which includes today's Al-Shahaniya municipality (ISO QA-SH, added 2017). An event placed in Al-Shahaniya is recorded under this unit at most. A statement about the map file, not about Qatar's administrative divisions.

precision_policy.reason: Qatar's gas processing and export, and most of its power and water plants, are concentrated in two industrial cities, so a municipality and a class together name the facility. Attacks and sabotage are recorded for the country, with no municipality, facility or operator. Other events are placed by municipality.

lng_terminal.basis: The iteration-20 Qatar researcher: all of the country's liquefaction is in one industrial complex. Not yet confirmed in the source audit; an entry here can only hold a record, never publish one.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

campaigns.name: Attacks on Qatari energy facilities, 2026
campaigns.status_basis: Attacks on energy facilities in Qatar were reported in 2026. No end to the wider war is reported, so the classification is uncertain, and uncertain is treated as active.

release_rule.text: Facility-specific restart, recovery or operating status for a record in a campaign is published only once the campaign is recorded as ended and 30 days have passed. While it is active the event itself is published; its facility status is not.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Qatar source-audit lane (iteration 19). CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read from the cited page or dataset in this session; vintages are mixed (2023-2025) and stated per row, and must not be combined into one 'current' picture. No value is later than a 2025 annual total, and none describes the state of any facility. Bases differ by source: country totals from EIA; operator totals from QatarEnergy's and KAHRAMAA's datasets on the Qatar Open Data Portal (CC BY 4.0). Capacities are nameplate or contracted figures and say nothing about operation. National aggregates only: no facility, train, plant or route figure is recorded. See docs/countries/QA_SOURCE_AUDIT.md. 8 figures newer than 2024 are withheld while the campaign policy applies.

significance: Natural gas made up 67.5% of Qatar's primary energy production in 2023 and crude oil and other petroleum liquids 32.5%; EIA marks coal as not applicable.
Qatar exported an estimated 4.4 Tcf of natural gas in 2024, about 3.6 Tcf of it as LNG (EIA, preliminary).
QatarEnergy reports LNG exports of between 77.8 and 79.3 million tonnes in each year from 2020 to 2025.
In 2023 Qatar generated 56 TWh of net electricity, virtually all from natural gas (EIA).

source_health.origin_rule: An origin is a wire service the citation names, else the website it sits on. Wikipedia and content aggregators are discovery aids and count as no origin. Republication a record does not name cannot be seen, so this can undercount independence but not overstate it.
source_health.first_party_excludes: Wikipedia, whatever role a record gives it
source_health.note: Describes the citations of the published events in this country. Not opened and not recorded are different: a researcher who did not record whether a source was opened is not evidence that it was not. Nothing here is comparable across countries and nothing here enters a number.

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: The citations of this system have not been link-checked.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year

onboarding_gate.label: Source registry with licence, cadence and reporting environment
onboarding_gate.note: Every source in use states its licence and publication cadence; the reporting environment is set. The event record itself is curated by hand, and its research passes are logged with the window each covered.
